subject: Next steps + request: decision owners & procurement path
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alison Park <alison.park@catalyst-retail.com>, Samir Khan <samir.k@catalyst-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps + request: decision owners & procurement path

Hi Alison / Samir — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + asks so we have alignment going into procurement:

- What we heard: POC to validate latency and cost at peak (holiday-level traffic), must pass PCI-adjacent data handling checks, and security needs to see audit/logging and key management options.
- Scope we proposed: 2-week pilot against 10k monthly active sessions, Redwood Dedicated with prefix caching enabled, performance SLAs during pilot for key routes.
- Success criteria (mutually agreed): <10% degradation on current latency percentiles, cost per active session under your target, and security sign-off on data flow.

Can you send the following so we can build the MAP and draft SOW?
1) Org chart or list of decision owners for procurement/finance/legal/security (PDF is fine).
2) Who is the economic buyer (name + best email) who signs budget?
3) High-level procurement timeline and any mandatory procurement docs (PO template, vendor questionnaire).
4) Security contact for SOC2 / network architecture review.

I attached a 1-page call notes doc and a simple draft MAP template (stub) to accelerate. Once I have the org chart I can draft the MAP with names and timeline and propose a short intro call that includes your procurement and security reps.

Thanks — really excited to move this forward.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
(555) 555-0142

Attachments: 2026-02-18-call-notes.pdf, Draft-MAP-v1.docx

Vanessa — good notes. Two quick internal items: 
- I’ll prep a short tech appendix (KV cache behavior, expected throughput) to attach to the MAP so security has something concrete.
- Pricing guardrails: keep the pilot under $12k to avoid additional approvals; if procurement asks for committed spend we can propose a 3-month reserved capacity option.

Ask them specifically for the procurement contact (name + email) and whether they require a vendor security questionnaire (we have a 1-day turnaround for our standard questionnaire).

Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Alison Park <alison.park@catalyst-retail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.k@catalyst-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps + request: decision owners & procurement path

Vanessa / Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Per call: attaching what I have now.

Attached: Catalyst-Org-Chart.pdf (high level), Procurement-Checklist.xlsx (procurement team checklist)

Quick answers: 
- Economic buyer: Rajesh Menon (CFO) — rajesh.menon@catalyst-retail.com. He’ll sign material contracts >$25k.
- Procurement lead: Samir Khan (cc’d) handles vendor onboarding and PO processing. He’ll own the procurement checklist.
- Security/compliance: Meghan Liu (meghan.liu@catalyst-retail.com) — she leads vendor security reviews and will want SOC2 reports, network diagrams, and KMS/HSM details.
- Legal: standard redlines negotiated by in-house counsel; they prefer to have an SOW + attachment with data handling clauses.
- Timeline: procurement window is ~2–3 weeks once SOW + pricing are submitted; security review can run in parallel but often needs 5 business days.

I can put together a short internal note and loop Rajesh if you want an intro. We’re targeting a decision by the end of March, but getting security and procurement comfortable before then is the gating factor.

On scheduling: Rajesh is available next Tue afternoon (2/24) for a 30-min intro if you can make it.

Thanks — attaching the files now.

— Alison Park
Director, Partnerships — Catalyst Retail
alison.park@catalyst-retail.com

Attachments: Catalyst-Org-Chart.pdf, Procurement-Checklist.xlsx

Thanks Alison — this is exactly what we needed. Next steps from our side and asks so we can keep momentum:

1) Rajesh / Meghan / Samir — would you join a 30-min alignment call next Tue 2/24? Proposed windows: 10:00–10:30 PT or 15:00–15:30 PT. Vanessa (me) + Marissa + Priyom will join from Redwood. Purpose: introduce team, confirm success criteria, outline procurement checklist items, and agree on timeline. Please reply with preferred slot and I’ll send an invite.

2) I’ve attached a first-pass MAP and a draft SOW outline (Draft-MAP-v1.docx). Marissa will add the technical appendix for security in the next 24 hours.

3) Please confirm Rajesh is the economic buyer who signs budget for the pilot (> $25k). If there’s someone else who needs to be on the signature path, tell us now so the MAP includes them.

4) If you have a vendor security questionnaire, please send it to me (vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com) or Meghan can take our standard questionnaire (we can turn it around in 24–48 hours for most fields).

We’ll keep the initial pilot scoped to ~$12k and can propose a committed reserved option if you prefer predictable throughput after pilot.

Look forward to the intro — I’ll prepare the calendar invite once you confirm time.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
